battle.name: 敘利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 奧龍特斯河谷與腓尼基海岸
battle.brief: 公元前274年至前200年，敘利亞淪為塞琉古與托勒密兩朝易手的拉鋸地。托勒密二世趁安條克一世與高盧人糳纏，奪下提爾與西頓；安條克二世以象兵反攻帕紐拉，托勒密三世再取安條克；安條克三世於拉多底亞逆轉，卻在前200年潘努斯敗陣。卡面長矛已讓位薩里沙，方陣傳統仍是兩軍骨架。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這是塞琉古王國與托勒密王國為爭奪敘利亞與地中海東岸而進行的長期角力，時間橫跨公元前274年至前200年，中間通常拆成五次敘利亞戰爭。塞琉古一方是亞歷山大繼業者中坐擁「亞洲」的一方：塞琉古一世於前312年回到巴比倫，前281年奠基安條克作首都，疆域自愛琴海東岸與安納托利亞南部，經幼發拉底河上游一直延伸到伊朗高原。塞琉古的權力靠「城市聯盟」維持，軍費與稅收主要來自安條克、阿帕梅亞、塞勒紐西亞·庇里亞等城市的歲入與關稅，國王之下由王室成員與各戰區將領（strategos）分頭統率。托勒密一方是前305年獨立的埃及王國，首都亞歷山大，領土含尼羅河三角洲、尼羅河谷、昔蘭尼加與塞浦路斯，並在安條克以北的黎凡特南部保有據點；其軍隊主體是埃及步兵方陣與弓手，輔以克里特弓手、希臘與高盧傭兵，並倚仗數量可觀的非洲象隊，糧秣由尼羅河的收成直接供給，錢糧調度是地中海諸國中最穩的一個。兩軍的爭奪點集中在奧龍特斯河谷與地中海東岸的腓尼基海岸：安條克扼住河谷上游，控扼內陸大道與通往美索不達米亞的商路；提爾、西頓、貝魯特三港扼住海上貿易與敘利亞門戶；拉多底亞與阿帕梅亞是內陸與海岸之間的轉運點。雙方也把外來力量拉進角力：塞琉古僱用高盧傭兵又與高盧人為敵，托勒密僱用高盧、克里特與伊庇魯斯兵；馬其頓王國在後期站在托勒密五世一邊，帕提亞與比克寧在安條克三世的東北邊境牽制塞琉古，羅馬則在戰爭末期直接改寫了這張地圖。
countriesEn: This was the long struggle of the Seleucid and the Ptolemaic kingdoms over Syria and the eastern Mediterranean littoral, running from 274 to 200 BC and conventionally divided into five Syrian Wars. On the Seleucid side stood the holder of Asia among Alexander's successors: Seleucus I, who was back at Babylon by 312 BC and founded Antioch as his capital in 281 BC, ruling from the eastern Aegean and southern Anatolia through the upper Euphrates to the Iranian plateau. Seleucid power rested on a league of cities; the money for the army came from the revenues and customs of Antioch, Apamea, Seleucia Pieria and the rest, and the king delegated command to members of the royal house and to strategoi appointed for each theatre of operations. The Ptolemaic side was the kingdom of Egypt, independent since 305 BC, with its capital at Alexandria and territory covering the Nile delta, the Nile valley, Cyrenaica and Cyprus, and with footholds in the southern Levant north of Antioch; the body of its army was the Egyptian phalanx of heavy infantry together with its archers, supported by Cretan archers, Greek and Galatian mercenaries and a considerable number of African elephants, and its grain came straight off the Nile, which gave it the steadiest money and supply system of any Mediterranean state. The points of contention lay in the valley of the Orontes and along the Phoenician coast: Antioch gripped the upper valley and the inland road to Mesopotamia, while Tyre, Sidon and Byblos gripped the sea trade and the gateway of Syria, and Laodicea and Apamea were the transshipment points between the interior and the coast. Both sides also drew outside powers into the contest. The Seleucids hired Galatian mercenaries while fighting the Galatians themselves, and the Ptolemies hired Galatian, Cretan and Epirote troops; Macedon later stood on Ptolemy V's side; Parthia and Bithynia pressed on Antiochus III's north-eastern frontier; and Rome rewrote the map outright once the wars had run their course.
people: 留下姓名的多數是兩朝的君主與將軍。塞琉古方面：安條克一世·索提爾（前三二一至前二六一年）是塞琉古一世之子，前二八〇年前後在比里亞的塞拉米斯敗於高盧人，退守安條克，前二七五年再在奧龍特斯河上游的科羅普西翁以象兵與弓手擊敗高盧軍，得了「索提爾」的名號；然而正是這場高盧戰爭把他的兵力和注意力釘在安納托利亞，無暇北顧，讓托勒密二世得以奪走腓尼基港口。安條克二世·提科斯（前二六一至前二四六年）以象立威，前二六一年在帕紐拉敗於托勒密二世並負傷退回安條克，前二四六年據說被一名高盧傭兵刺殺。安條克三世·大帝（前二二三至前一八七年）靠托勒密三世的協助奪回王位，前二四六至前二四五年的拉多底亞之戰中大敗托勒密四世並一度將其俘獲，前二〇〇年潘努斯之戰卻在取勝之後戰死沙場。托勒密方面：托勒密二世·費拉德爾福斯（前二八五至前二四六年）是開國者托勒密一世的繼承人，娶胞妹阿爾西諾厄二世為后，延續亞歷山大家族兄妹相婚的傳統，他完成了提爾與西頓的奪取，並在第二次敘利亞戰爭中兩度圍困安條克。托勒密三世·優厄革特斯（前二四六至前二二二年）在貝魯特擊敗安條克二世並攻入安條克，皇后貝雷妮刻二世出身昔蘭尼加，他本人也曾出兵支援安條克三世奪位。托勒密五世·埃普托法尼斯（前二〇四至前一八〇年）是潘努斯的敗者，與姊姊克雷奧佩特拉一世一同捲入塞琉古王室的廢立。另有三人特別值得記下：潘努斯之戰中替托勒密五世指揮希臘傭兵的馬其頓尼亞斯（曼提奈亞人），他打垮了安條克三世的左翼，卻在埃及被清算；塞琉古四世·菲利帕托爾娶了托勒密五世的姊姊克雷奧佩特拉一世，使兩個王朝以王室婚姻短暫綁在一起；而波利比奧斯《歷史》第五卷與第十八卷是這場角力留下最完整的戰史記錄。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive belong to the kings and generals of the two houses. On the Seleucid side: Antiochus I Soter, from 321 to 261 BC, was the son of Seleucus I. Around 280 BC he was beaten by the Galatians at Selaemis in Pieria and fell back on Antioch, and in 275 BC he beat them again at Corupissium on the upper Orontes, using elephants and archers, which is where the title Soter comes from; but it was precisely that war against the Galatians that pinned his troops and his attention in Anatolia, so that he could not look north, and Ptolemy II was able to take the Phoenician ports. Antiochus II Theicus, from 261 to 246 BC, made his name with elephants; in 261 BC he was defeated at Panarus by Ptolemy II, was himself wounded, and withdrew to Antioch, and in 246 BC he is said to have been killed by a Galatian mercenary. Antiochus III the Great, from 223 to 187 BC, recovered his throne with the help of Ptolemy III, won the Battle of Laodicea in 246 or 245 BC and for a moment held Ptolemy IV prisoner, and then, in 200 BC, was killed on the field of Panus after winning it. On the Ptolemaic side: Ptolemy II Philadelphus, from 285 to 246 BC, was the successor of the founder Ptolemy I and married his own sister Arsinoe II, continuing the sibling marriage of the house of Alexander; it was he who took Tyre and Sidon and who twice invested Antioch during the Second Syrian War. Ptolemy III Euergetes, from 246 to 222 BC, beat Antiochus II at Berytus and entered Antioch, his queen Berenice II coming from Cyrenaica, and he himself had put men in the field to support Antiochus III's claim to the throne. Ptolemy V Epiphanes, from 204 to 180 BC, lost Panus, and he and his sister Cleopatra I were drawn into the making and unmaking of the Seleucid succession. Three more deserve to be singled out: Macedonius of Mantinea, who commanded the Greek mercenaries for Ptolemy V at Panus and beat the left wing of Antiochus III, only to be liquidated in Egypt; Seleucus IV Philopator, who married Ptolemy V's sister Cleopatra I and so tied the two houses together for a moment by royal marriage; and Polybius, whose fifth and eighteenth books of the Histories preserve the fullest tactical account of the whole contest.
kits: 卡面上這件斯巴達長矛（dory）得先放對位置：兩米長的木桿，前端裝青銅或鐵矛頭，槍尾套一枚銅箍以便落地撐持，是古典重裝步兵的標誌裝備。但到了前二七四年，希臘化世界的主力長矛已是薩里沙，即馬其頓方陣所用的四至六公尺長矛，可以從後排越過前排肩甲刺出；dory 在實戰中退居輕裝步兵、衛兵與登陸部隊的制式武器，只在「方陣」這個技術譜系裡保留象徵位置。卡面兵器代表的是骨架，而不是當時的制式長矛。塞琉古與托勒密共用的方陣裝備包括：希臘式青銅胸甲與鱗甲，或埃及式的亞麻鱗甲，兩軍的重裝步兵都披亞麻甲；橢圓或圓形的希臘大盾（aspis）與較小的方盾；頭盔多為青銅的科林斯式與希臘式冠頂盔；近身兵器是短劍與雙刃劍，埃及那邊還留著月牙形單刃劍的舊式。弓箭是主要的投射火力，克里特弓、敘利亞弓與埃及弓各有不同的射程與慣用陣位，弩砲（chiroballistra）則用於攻城與守城，可把火球拋射到對岸。象是這場戰爭最具辨識度的裝備：托勒密王朝養數百頭非洲象，塞琉古則自印度取得印度象（塞琉古一世前303年與孔雀王朝訂約時換得一頭，此後在本土繁殖），並為象頭與象身包覆金屬板、在象背架塔。攻城裝備中最特別的是托勒密二世圍提爾時修築的堤壩：他在海峽最窄處填土築路，把海島城市與大陸隔斷，再用海軍封住另一半的港門，圍了七個月，最後以斷糧迫降；塞琉古軍則用攻城塔、撞柱與填土斜坡。安條克二世在安條克城下的河面上還用過能投射燃燒火丸的器械，波利比奧斯記載它燒毀了奧龍特斯河中相當一部分埃及船隻，而托勒密的船工以濕泥覆船防火。高盧傭兵帶著雙刃大劍、鐵盔與大盾上陣，不着甲胄，靠衝鋒與單兵格鬥取勝。
kitsEn: The Spartan dory on the card has to be placed correctly first: a wooden shaft two metres long, with a bronze or iron head at the front and a bronze collar at the butt so that it could be planted in the ground and supported, it was the emblematic weapon of the classical hoplite. But by 274 BC the standard long weapon of the Hellenistic world was the sarissa, the four to six metre pike of the Macedonian phalanx, which could be levelled over the shoulders of the files in front; the dory had sunk to the standard weapon of light infantry, of guards and of landing parties, and survived in the iconography of the phalanx rather than in the line of battle. What the card represents is the skeleton, not the regulation pike of the day. The equipment shared by the two armies in the phalanx included Greek bronze cuirasses and scale armour, or Egyptian linen scale armour, for the heavy infantry of either side wore linen; elliptical or round Greek shields, the aspis, and the smaller pelte; helmets mostly of bronze in the Corinthian and Greek styles with a crest; and close-combat weapons of short swords and double-edged blades, with the old Egyptian single-edged curved sword still in use on the Ptolemaic side. Missiles were the archers: the Cretan, Syrian and Egyptian bows each had their own reach and their own place in the line, while the cheiroballistra served in sieges and defences and could lob fireballs across a river. The elephant was the most recognisable piece of equipment in the whole contest: the Ptolemies kept several hundred African elephants, while the Seleucids drew theirs from India, Seleucus I having received one in the treaty with the Mauryan court in 303 BC and the herds then breeding in Seleucid territory, and the head and body were plated with metal and a tower set on the back. The most remarkable item of siege equipment was the causeway built by Ptolemy II during the siege of Tyre: he filled in the narrowest point of the channel to cut the island city off from the mainland, closed the other half of the harbour with the fleet, and after seven months forced a surrender by cutting off supplies. The Seleucid army used siege towers, battering rams and earthen ramps instead. Antiochus II also used a machine that threw burning fireballs against the river below Antioch; Polybius records that it burned a considerable part of the Egyptian fleet in the Orontes, and that the Egyptian crews answered it by coating their ships with wet clay. The Galatian mercenaries came with their own long double-edged swords, iron helmets and large shields, without armour, and won by charging and by fighting singly.
tactics: 七十四年的作戰樣貌並不單一，但可歸成三種。第一種是圍城，提爾的圍攻是最典型的樣本：托勒密二世沒有直接強攻海島，而是在海峽最窄處填土築堤，切斷提爾與大陸唯一的陸路，同時以海軍封閉南面的港口，然後長期駐紮、步步逼近，七個月後提爾接受條件。城內靠武庫、井水與外海的漁獲撐到最後，圍城方靠埃及運來的穀物與工程器材維持，這是一場純粹靠土木與海運決定的消耗戰。第二種是野戰會戰，奧龍特斯河谷的平原地形適合重裝步兵方陣展開。帕紐拉之戰（前二六一年）裡，安條克二世把象隊放在陣前，試圖以象衝散托勒密的希臘步兵，方陣正面因此被壓彎，安條克二世本人也在混戰中負傷；托勒密二世沒有追擊，讓對手退回合城。貝魯特之戰（前二五二年）裡，托勒密三世用方陣與兩翼騎兵對付安條克二世，先穩住中央，再以騎兵繞擊，迫使對方退回安條克。拉多底亞之戰（前二四六至前二四五年）形勢相反，安條克三世靠右翼迂迴與中央方陣的正面壓力分割托勒密四世的隊形，埃及象群在混戰中失控，成為混亂的來源；托勒密四世被俘。第三種是兩翼衝擊與王室直接指揮的會戰，潘努斯之戰（前二〇〇年）是典範：安條克三世把象隊與精銳放在左翼，中央是縱深方陣，右翼交給馬其頓尼亞斯率領的希臘傭兵；托勒密五世把兩個方陣放在前線，兩翼配克里特與希臘傭兵。會戰先在右翼的騎兵與步兵之間接觸：托勒密的右翼一度退卻，安條克三世的左翼乘勢深入，象群受希臘步兵的長矛與吶喊驚散，反過來衝垮自己的陣線，安條克三世在追擊中頭部被一枚投石擊中（一說為標槍），當日身亡；托勒密五世退向埃及。後勤決定這些會戰能打多久：托勒密軍隊自亞歷山大經海路與陸路把尼羅河的穀物運到奧龍特斯河谷再轉往前線，直線距離約一千五百公里；塞琉古的補給靠安條克與阿帕梅亞的城市稅收與內陸道路。希臘化軍隊的另一個特徵是「縱深」：方陣的縱深與替補制度讓前排倒下後由後排補上，安條克三世還在方陣後設置投射部隊，這是托勒密軍隊在潘努斯受挫的原因之一。
tacticsEn: The shape of the fighting changed over the seventy-four years, but it can be reduced to three kinds. The first is the siege, of which the investment of Tyre is the type case. Ptolemy II did not assault the island directly; he filled in the narrowest point of the channel to cut the one land route between Tyre and the mainland, closed the harbour on the other side with the fleet, and then sat down and pressed in by degrees, and after seven months Tyre took his terms. The city held out on its arsenal, its wells and the fishing of the open sea, while the besiegers lived off grain shipped from Egypt and on their engineering stores: a contest decided purely by earthworks and by sea transport. The second kind is the pitched battle fought on the open ground of the Orontes valley, which suits the deployment of a heavy phalanx. At Panarus in 261 BC Antiochus II put his elephants in front, hoping to disorder Ptolemy's Greek infantry, and the face of the phalanx was bent by them, and Antiochus II himself was wounded in the mêlée; Ptolemy II did not pursue, and let his opponent fall back on his walled city. At the Battle of Berytus in 252 BC Ptolemy III met Antiochus II with phalanx and cavalry on the flanks, steadied his centre first and then turned the cavalry round his side, forcing the king back to Antioch. The Battle of Laodicea in 246 or 245 BC went the other way: Antiochus III split Ptolemy IV's formation with a turning movement on his right and the pressure of his central phalanx, the Egyptian elephants broke loose in the confusion and became the source of it, and Ptolemy IV was taken prisoner. The third kind is the meeting engagement decided on the wings and commanded by the king in person, of which Panus in 200 BC is the type case: Antiochus III put the elephants and the picked troops on his left, the deep phalanx in the centre and the Greek mercenaries under Macedonius on his right, while Ptolemy V put two phalanxes in front with Cretan and Greek mercenaries on the wings. The action began on the right, where cavalry and foot came into contact; the Ptolemaic right gave ground for a time, Antiochus III's left pushed in after them, and the elephants were startled by the long pikes and the cries of the Greek foot and broke back through their own line, and Antiochus III, in the pursuit, was struck in the head by a stone thrown by hand, or by a javelin according to another account, and died that day, while Ptolemy V withdrew towards Egypt. Logistics set the length of these battles: the Ptolemaic armies moved the grain of the Nile from Alexandria to the Orontes valley and thence to the front by sea and land, a straight-line distance of about fifteen hundred kilometres, while the Seleucids drew on the city revenues of Antioch and Apamea and on the inland roads. The other feature of a Hellenistic army was depth: the files of the phalanx were deep enough that the front rank could be replaced as it fell, and Antiochus III stationed missile troops behind his phalanx, which was one of the reasons the Ptolemaic army came off badly at Panus.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是波利比奧斯《歷史》留下的戰役兵力：潘努斯之戰（前二〇〇年）他記安條克三世有步兵約六千、騎兵約五千，托勒密五世有步兵約二千、騎兵約四千，馬其頓援助的傭兵在數千人量級，他特意指出那是一場規模不大的會戰，後世在「以多取勝」的敘述中常把它誇大。第二類是圍城與行程的可量度事實：提爾圍城歷時七個月；托勒密二世在第二次敘利亞戰爭中圍安條克約半年，因腓尼基戰事與後方牽制而於前二五九年前後解圍退回埃及；托勒密三世在貝魯特之戰後再度佔領安條克；從亞歷山大到安條克直線距離約一千五百公里，安條克到拉多底亞約六十公里、到貝魯特約一百二十公里、到提爾約二百三十公里；前二九〇年的馬格尼西亞之戰後，羅馬迫使安條克三世放棄小亞細亞，這是整場角力的終點而非開端。第三類是規模估算，必須打折：安條克二世在安條克常備兵員有「七萬五千」之說，但那是全境守備與後備的合計，真正投入野戰的只是其中一部；托勒密二世即位時的象群有「約八百頭」的說法，也有較保守的估計認為在數百頭以下；安條克三世在拉多底亞方向的投入常被描述為數萬人量級，具體數字在古典文獻中互不一致。時間跨度反而最可靠：從前二七四年到前二〇〇年，敘利亞的爭奪打了七十四年，通常拆成五次敘利亞戰爭，計第一次前二七四至前二七一年、第二次前二六〇至前二五五年、第三次前二四五至前二四一年、第四次前二一九至前二一七年、第五次前二〇二至前二〇〇年，另有一場前二四六至前二四一年的拉多底亞戰爭夾在其間，多數也歸入同一系列。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is the troop strength Polybius records for the battles themselves: at Panus in 200 BC he gives Antiochus III about six thousand foot and five thousand horse, and Ptolemy V about two thousand foot and four thousand horse, with the mercenaries sent by Macedon numbering a few thousand, and he points out expressly that this was a small engagement, though later narratives of a war won by weight of numbers have habitually inflated it. The second class consists of measurable facts about sieges and distances: the siege of Tyre lasted seven months; Ptolemy II's investment of Antioch in the Second Syrian War ran for about half a year and was lifted around 259 BC because of trouble in Phoenicia and on his own rear; Ptolemy III occupied Antioch again after Berytus; the straight-line distance from Alexandria to Antioch is about fifteen hundred kilometres, and from Antioch to Laodicea about sixty, to Byblos about a hundred and twenty, to Tyre about two hundred and thirty; and after the Battle of Magnesia in 190 BC Rome forced Antiochus III to give up Asia Minor, which is the end of this contest rather than its beginning. The third class is estimate, and has to be discounted: there is a figure of seventy-five thousand for the troops Antiochus II kept at Antioch, but that is the total of garrisons and reserves across the realm, and only a fraction of it ever fought in the field; there is a claim that Ptolemy II had something like eight hundred elephants at his accession, and more conservative estimates put the herds in the hundreds; and the force Antiochus III committed in the Laodicea direction is usually described as numbering tens of thousands, with the classical sources disagreeing. The one span of time that is reliable is the length of the whole contest: from 274 to 200 BC the struggle over Syria ran for seventy-four years, and is conventionally divided into five Syrian Wars, the first from 274 to 271 BC, the second from 260 to 255, the third from 245 to 241, the fourth from 219 to 217 and the fifth from 202 to 200, with a Laodicean War of 246 to 241 BC lying between them that is also usually reckoned into the same series.
cause: 要理解這場角力，得回到前323年亞歷山大死後的繼業者戰爭。帝國沒有可靠的繼承人，幾位部將在十年的分割中把版圖切成三塊：托勒密一世守住埃及、塞浦路斯與黎凡特南部；塞琉古一世最後取得「亞洲」，即兩河與安納托利亞；安提柯一系在馬其頓。前三〇五年前後托勒密在埃及稱王，敘利亞就成了兩家的必爭之地：它既是托勒密的北部屏障，一旦塞琉古控制了腓尼基港口與奧龍特斯河谷，埃及的邊境等於被推到尼羅河三角洲的門口；它也是塞琉古的戰略心臟，安條克正建在奧龍特斯河畔，控制敘利亞等於同時握有內陸大道、幼發拉底河上游的東岸與地中海東岸的門戶。兩個王朝的合法性敘事也互不相容：塞琉古自認為亞歷山大亞洲行省的直接繼承者，托勒密則以「本土王朝」自居，把埃及的古老神祇與法老傳統作為自己的合法性來源，誰拿下敘利亞，誰就是在宣稱自己才是帝國的正統繼承人。直接導火線則在安條克一世身上。前二八〇年前後，高盧人越過安納托利亞大舉東進，安條克在比里亞的塞拉米斯敗北，退守安條克，前二七五年才在科羅普西翁靠象兵與弓手打敗高盧人；塞琉古的腹地因此整個淪為戰場，國王的注意力、兵力和錢糧全被釘在安納托利亞，敘利亞的防線只剩寡兵。這正是第一次敘利亞戰爭開局時的形勢：托勒密二世幾乎沒有遇到像樣的抵抗，就把提爾、西頓一路拿下。此外塞琉古王室的內爭也一直在消耗這份力量：安條克一世的兄弟安條克·希拉克斯爭奪王位，遺產戰爭拖了十多年，敘利亞與美索不達米亞的城邑在內鬥中反覆易手，國力還沒有恢復，第二次敘利亞戰爭就開打；而托勒密王朝內部後來也出現王位與宮廷派系的爭奪，說明角力的雙方都不是穩定的機器。
causeEn: To understand this contest one has to go back to the Wars of the Diadochi that followed the death of Alexander in 323 BC. The empire had no reliable heir, and in a decade of partition the leading generals cut it into three: Ptolemy I held Egypt, Cyprus and the southern Levant; Seleucus I at last secured Asia, the two riverlands and Anatolia; and the Antigonids held Macedon. Around 305 BC Ptolemy made himself king in Egypt, and Syria became the prize neither side could leave alone. It was the northern shield of the Ptolemies, for once the Seleucids held the Phoenician ports and the valley of the Orontes the frontier of Egypt was pushed to the door of the Nile delta; and it was the strategic heart of the Seleucids, since Antioch itself stood on the Orontes, and control of Syria meant control of the inland road, of the eastern bank of the upper Euphrates and of the entrance to the eastern Mediterranean at once. The two courts also carried incompatible stories of legitimacy: the Seleucids claimed to be the direct successors of Alexander's Asian provinces, while the Ptolemies presented themselves as a native dynasty, resting their claim on the ancient gods and the pharaonic tradition of Egypt, and whoever took Syria was asserting that he, and not his rival, was the true inheritor of the empire. The immediate trigger lay with Antiochus I. Around 280 BC the Galatians poured east across Anatolia, Antiochus was beaten north of Selaemis in Pieria and fell back on Antioch, and only in 275 BC did he break the Galatians at Corupissium with elephants and archers. The whole Seleucid hinterland became a battlefield, the king's attention, soldiers and money were all pinned to Anatolia, and the Syrian line was held by a handful of troops. That was the situation at the opening of the First Syrian War: Ptolemy II met almost no serious resistance and took Tyre and Sidon in turn. The internal quarrels of the Seleucid house were draining that strength all the while: Antiochus Hierax, brother of Antiochus I, disputed the throne, the war of inheritance dragged on for more than a decade, and the cities of Syria and Mesopotamia changed hands repeatedly in that fratricide, so that before the Seleucid state had recovered the Second Syrian War began; and inside the Ptolemaic house the struggle over the throne and the court factions would later break out as well, which shows that neither side was a stable machine.
impact: 七十四年的角力沒有任何一方永久得到敘利亞，卻重塑了東地中海。制度上，安條克在這一階段完成希臘化城市的重建：塞勒紐西亞·庇里亞的新城、阿帕梅亞的重鎮、安條克本身的都會規模，構成「城市聯邦」式的塞琉古王國骨架，國家的稅收、兵源與合法性都掛在城市上；托勒密王朝則把埃及的傳統神權與王位綁在一起，塑造出「埃及本土王朝」的政治想像，這一想像在後來羅馬人接受托勒密王朝時被再次使用。軍事上，這段角力把希臘化方陣打磨成主力：多列縱深、投射武器前置、象與傭兵擔任突破任務、海上封鎖與堤壩圍城的技術都在這一時期成熟；安條克二世用投射火丸的器械、托勒密二世用填土堤壩切斷海島城市的做法，都成為後來攻城戰的教科書案例。塞琉古的象兵與燃燒劑、托勒密的非洲象與埃及弓手，也在此後的羅馬—敘利亞戰爭裡被人拿來比較。經濟與文化上，敘利亞沿海的腓尼基港市在兩強的競爭中被反覆爭奪，也因此累積了地中海世界最密集的商船網絡之一；安條克與貝魯特承接了亞歷山大城的學術傳統，成為希臘化東方的知識節點；敘利亞種植的棉花與酒大量流入埃及，尼羅河的穀物與安條克的稅收則反向輸往地中海。政治版圖上，最大的長遠後果是羅馬的介入：前二〇〇年潘努斯之後，塞琉古在內戰中折損，羅馬於前一九二年迫使安條克三世退出小亞細亞，前一九〇年馬格尼西亞之戰更把塞琉古的亞洲行省限制在托羅斯山脈以東；敘利亞從此變成羅馬在東方的門戶與邊防，安條克是羅馬東方軍團的駐地，也是後來羅馬與帕提亞拉鋒的前線。漢尼拔時代之後希臘化世界第一次大規模的國家級戰爭，就此以「兩個王朝都沒有滅亡、但一方被打出敘利亞」的方式收場。
impactEn: Seventy-four years of struggle left the permanent possession of Syria to neither side, but they reshaped the eastern Mediterranean. Institutionally, Antioch was rebuilt in this period as a Hellenistic city: the new foundation of Seleucia Pieria, the strong garrison city of Apamea, the metropolitan scale of Antioch itself, and these made up the skeleton of a Seleucid state organised as a league of cities, with the revenue, the manpower and the legitimacy of the realm all hung upon those cities; the Ptolemaic house meanwhile bound the traditional gods of Egypt to its throne and built the political imagination of a native Egyptian dynasty, an idea the Romans were later to take up again when they accepted the Ptolemies. Militarily, the contest polished the Hellenistic phalanx into the main instrument of war: depth of files, missile troops in front, elephants and mercenaries given the task of breaking a line, and the technique of blockade by sea and of siege by causeway all matured in this period, and Antiochus II's fire-throwing machine and Ptolemy II's earthen dam across the channel of an island city both became textbook cases of siegecraft. The Seleucid elephants and burning mixtures and the Ptolemaic African elephants and Egyptian archers were long afterwards compared with one another in the Roman-Syrian wars. Economically and culturally, the Phoenician ports of the Syrian coast, fought over repeatedly by the two powers, accumulated one of the densest merchant fleets in the Mediterranean world; Antioch and Byblos took over the scholarly traditions of Alexandria and became the intellectual nodes of the Hellenistic east; the cotton and the wine of Syria flowed into Egypt in quantity, while the grain of the Nile and the revenues of Antioch flowed the other way. Politically, the largest long-term consequence was the arrival of Rome: after Panus in 200 BC the Seleucids had been worn down by their own civil war, Rome forced Antiochus III out of Asia Minor in 192 BC, and the battle of Magnesia in 190 BC confined the Seleucid Asian provinces to the east of the Taurus; Syria became from then on the gateway and the frontier of Rome in the east, Antioch the station of the Roman army of the east and the forward line of the later Roman-Parthian rivalry. The first great state-level war of the Hellenistic world after the age of Hannibal was thus closed with neither dynasty destroyed but one of them driven out of Syria.
result: 把七十年的帳算清楚，結果是沒有單一勝者。敘利亞在這段時間裡至少五次易手：托勒密二世拿下提爾與西頓（前二七四至前二七一年），安條克二世在帕紐拉奪回主動權（前二六一年），托勒密二世一度圍困安條克又因腓尼基戰事與後方牽制撤圍（前二五九至前二五五年），托勒密三世在貝魯特擊敗安條克二世並入據安條克（前二五二至前二四五年），安條克三世在拉多底亞大勝並一度俘獲托勒密四世（前二四六至前二四五年），前二〇一年塞琉古四世在拉班河擊敗托勒密五世，最後前二〇〇年潘努斯之戰又由安條克三世取勝，卻戰死當場。勝負真正的轉折點不在任何一場會戰，而在塞琉古王室的內戰與羅馬的到來。前二〇一年塞琉古四世在拉班河取勝，又娶了托勒密五世的姊姊克雷奧佩特拉一世，政治上正走到頂點；但他的兄長安條克三世仍在位，兄弟倆的內爭把塞琉古的軍力與國庫在數年內耗掉大半，羅馬隨即乘虛而入，前一九〇年馬格尼西亞之戰後，安條克三世被迫放棄小亞細亞與歐洲的殘餘權益，敘利亞變成羅馬庇護下的一組自由城市，敘利亞戰爭也在前二〇〇年前後落幕。對兩個王朝的長期命運而言，這場角力是分水嶺：托勒密王朝失去了海外的領土重心，退回尼羅河谷，靠埃及的財富延續到前三十年，最後亡於屋大維；塞琉古王朝把重心退到美索不達米亞與伊朗高原，延續到前六三年而為羅馬所滅。對武器與戰術史而言，它的成果更實在：薩里沙方陣、象兵投射、火丸投射器、堤壩圍城與海上封鎖，都在這七十年的反覆交手中被驗證、被改良，後來馬其頓戰爭中塞琉古與托勒密對付羅馬的軍隊之所以仍具戰力，很大一部分技術底子就是在這段敘利亞的拉鋸裡打下來的。
resultEn: Set the account of seventy years straight, and the result is that there was no single victor. Syria changed hands at least five times in that span: Ptolemy II took Tyre and Sidon from 274 to 271 BC; Antiochus II recovered the initiative at Panarus in 261; Ptolemy II invested Antioch and then withdrew around 259 to 255 because of trouble in Phoenicia and on his own rear; Ptolemy III beat Antiochus II at Berytus and occupied Antioch from 252 to 245; Antiochus III won at Laodicea from 246 to 245 and for a moment held Ptolemy IV prisoner; Seleucus IV defeated Ptolemy V at the river Labicus in 201; and finally Panus in 200 was won by Antiochus III, who was killed on the field. The real turning point lay in no single battle, but in the civil war inside the Seleucid house and in the arrival of Rome. In 201 BC Seleucus IV was victorious at the Labicus and had married Ptolemy V's sister Cleopatra I, and politically he stood at the summit of his power; but his elder brother Antiochus III was still on the throne, and the fratricide between the two brothers drained the Seleucid army and treasury within a few years, and Rome came in on the strength of that: after the battle of Magnesia in 190 BC Antiochus III was compelled to give up his remaining claims in Asia Minor and Europe, and Syria became a group of free cities under Roman protection, and with Panus the Syrian Wars came to an end around 200 BC. For the long-term fortunes of the two dynasties this contest was a watershed: the Ptolemies lost their overseas centre of gravity, withdrew into the Nile valley, lived on the wealth of Egypt until 30 BC and finally perished under Octavian; the Seleucids shifted their weight back to Mesopotamia and the Iranian plateau and lasted until 63 BC, when Rome took them too. For the history of weapons and tactics its results are more solid: the sarissa phalanx, missile fire from elephants, the fireball projector, the causeway siege and the blockade by sea were all tested, corrected and improved in the repeated exchanges of these seventy years, and it is largely because the technical groundwork was laid in this long Syrian grind that the Seleucid and Ptolemaic armies of the Macedonian wars were still worth fighting when they faced Rome.
